summary: Verified fix for chat date-bucketing / chronological ordering after page refresh. Backend unit tests (2/2) confirm _persist_chat_turns() now stamps the user turn with self._started_at (loop-start time) instead of time.time() at completion. Frontend unit tests (11/11, including 4 new t_sort_* cases) confirm sortMessagesByTimestamp is stable, respects ties, handles missing ts, and is a no-op on already-sorted arrays. Code review confirms it is correctly wired into ChatPanel.jsx's history-load useEffect (line 1518) and that `ts` is preserved on hydrated turn objects (line 1526). Live UI: sent messages render in correct order under a single 'Today' divider before refresh. Full end-to-end refresh assertion within the SAME session was blocked by an unrelated preview-env issue (GitHub App revoked → project connection unavailable → backend replies with a placeholder and doesn't persist non-loop user turns), so post-refresh the just-sent messages disappear entirely. That is orthogonal to the ordering/date-bucket bug and does not invalidate the fix — the fix's correctness is proven by the unit tests + code wiring.

integration_issues.flow: Chat message persistence in preview env
integration_issues.issue: When the active project's GitHub App is revoked/disconnected, sending a normal (non-loop) chat message shows a placeholder assistant reply ('connection to your website's code isn't available right now') and the user turn appears NOT to be persisted (post-refresh the message is absent from /chat/history for the same session_id). This blocks end-to-end verification of any chat-history behavior in the preview env. Root cause is the environment's stale GitHub connection, not the date-bucket fix itself.

action_items: OPTIONAL: In preview env, reconnect the AUREM GitHub App to the demo project (aurem-demo/frontend) so end-to-end chat persistence works and testers can visually re-verify the refresh-order/date-bucket fix live. Not blocking — fix correctness is proven by unit tests.
OPTIONAL: 6 console errors (403) surface on chat page load due to the same revoked-GH-token condition; these disappear once the GitHub App is reconnected.
critical_code_review_comments: sortMessagesByTimestamp is stable and correctly falls back to original index on ties/missing ts — good defensive design as a general reload-time safety net beyond the specific loop-pause case.
Frontend history-load hydration explicitly preserves `ts: typeof t.ts === 'number' ? t.ts : undefined` (ChatPanel.jsx:1526) — necessary for the sort to have real values to work on. Confirmed present.

loop_engine._persist_chat_turns fix uses `self._started_at` (captured at LoopEngine construction) for the user turn and `now` for the assistant turn — semantically correct: user prompt existed at construction, assistant reply only exists at completion.

Minor: /chat/history returns raw stored order (no backend-side sort). Frontend sort is now the single source of ordering truth on reload. Acceptable, but the codebase could add a defensive `.sort` on the /chat/history backend for extra safety (cheap, would prevent client-only sorters like curl/scripts from seeing wrong order).

success_rate.frontend: 100% (11/11 unit tests pass; UI pre-refresh sanity check pass; full e2e refresh blocked by unrelated env)

context_for_next_testing_agent: For a true end-to-end verification of the reload ordering fix in the preview env, first reconnect the demo project's GitHub App (currently revoked, causing all non-loop chat sends to return a placeholder response without persisting the turn). Once persistence works, the flow is: (1) log in test@aurem.dev, (2) send 3 chat messages in the current session, (3) capture localStorage['aurem.chat.sessionId'], (4) refresh, (5) verify the same session_id is restored, and that /api/aurem-dev/chat/history?session_id=<id> returns the messages with monotonically non-decreasing ts values, and the UI renders them under a single 'Today' divider in send order. Note: the frontend uses baseURL `${REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL}/api/aurem-dev`, so the correct absolute path is /api/aurem-dev/chat/history — NOT /api/chat/history (which 404s).
rca of the issue: Original bug RCA (already fixed by main agent, verified by this run): services/loop_engine.py._persist_chat_turns() only ran at loop TERMINAL state. When a loop was paused for approval (plan/ship gate) and later resumed hours/days later, the user's original prompt was persisted with `time.time()` at COMPLETION time instead of the loop's real submission time, causing (a) the turn to be $push'd at the end of chat_sessions.turns (wrong chronological position) and (b) date-bucketing to place old prompts under 'Today' instead of their actual day. Fix: user turn now uses self._started_at (captured at LoopEngine __init__); assistant turn keeps `now`. Frontend belt-and-suspenders: sortMessagesByTimestamp() stable-sorts by ts on history reload so any out-of-order backend push still renders correctly.
